marks.gloss_en: כתיב התם ולקחתם אגודת אזוב (Shemot 12:22), וכתיב הכא ולקחתם לכם ביום הראשון (Vayikra 23:40): מה להלן באגודה, אף כאן באגודה
ורבנן: לקיחה מלקיחה לא ילפינן -- the Rabbis do not accept the gezera shava; it is blocked in their framework only (= p_rabanan_lo_yalfi_lekicha)
and the Rabbis: we do not learn 'taking' from 'taking'
מכאן אמרו -- the ruling on the trellised plants is drawn from תעשה ולא מן העשוי
if he hung them and afterwards cut the ends of their threads -- they are invalid
ובפלוגתא דהני תנאי, דתניא: לולב בין אגוד בין שאינו אגוד כשר; רבי יהודה אומר אגוד כשר, שאינו אגוד פסול -- the binding question is a known tannaitic dispute
or say: if we hold the lulav requires binding, all agree we learn lulav from sukkah; here they dispute this: one holds it requires binding, the other that it does not
מיתיבי: תלאן ולא פסק ראשי חוטין שלהן -- פסולין. מאי לאו פסולין לעולם, ותיובתא דרב?
אמר לך רב: מאי פסולין -- פסולין עד שיפסקו (= p_pesulin_ad_sheyipaseku)
if he hung them and did not cut the ends of their threads -- they are invalid
אמר לך רב: הכא במאי עסקינן -- דשלפינהו שלופי, דלא מינכרא עשיה דידהו: he pulled them off, so their making is not noticeable
מאי איריא משום תעשה ולא מן העשוי? תיפוק ליה דמחוברין נינהו! -- uncut, they are attached to the ground and invalid for that reason; the taaseh reason would be idle
(candidate) the baraita speaks of one who did not cut them
אי רבי יהודה, כי לא אגדו אמאי כשר? -- for him an unbound lulav is invalid
אי רבנן, אמאי מצוה? -- for them binding is not required at all
a lulav -- it is a mitzva to bind it
lest you say we require [a single] corner at the time of the threading, and there is none -- it teaches us [that it is not required]
Rav Matna: the case happened to me, and I came before Mar Shmuel, and he said to me: invalid forever
if he transgressed and picked them -- invalid; the words of R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak
(they supposed) all agree the lulav requires binding
(entertained) the tannaim dispute this: the validator holds that of sukkah we say their cutting is their making, and of lulav their picking is their making; the invalidator holds we do not
no: all agree that of sukkah we do not say their cutting is their making
Reish Lakish: the verse says 'and a mist went up from the earth' (Bereshit 2:6)
חג הסוכות תעשה לך -- sukkah is juxtaposed to the chagiga: as the chagiga is a thing not susceptible to impurity whose growth is from the ground, so too the sukkah (as reported by Rav Dimi)

R' Yochanan per Rav Dimi: 'the festival of sukkot you shall make for yourself' (Devarim 16:13) juxtaposes sukkah to the festival-offering; as the chagiga is not susceptible to impurity and grows from the ground, so the sukkah
the stam: the mist-derivation works for the one who says the desert sukkot were clouds of glory -- R' Eliezer
